summary.text: 來, “come,” began as a picture of wheat and was borrowed to write a similar-sounding word for coming. Its shape therefore belongs to the plant, while its common meaning belongs to the borrowed word. Wheat itself is now written 麥.

formation.text: A wheat pictograph was reused for the word “come.”

components.text: The whole character is a plant outline: ear, leaves, stem and roots. Its person-like inner strokes are not separately added people.

history.text: The crop use and the movement use both occur in oracle-bone writing. Some forms have an extra stroke at the top, but that stroke does not consistently distinguish wheat from coming. It cannot safely be assigned a fixed meaning.

uncertainties.text: The precise division of early uses between 來 and 麥 remains debated. One proposal gives 麥 an earlier movement sense and suggests that the two characters’ uses changed places.
